steps.title: Cold key-on: read the RFHUB first
steps.why: Before any other traffic, so a B1040-64 appearing is caught and not caused by our own reads.
steps.preconditions: Car cold, key on, nothing else on the bus yet.

steps.title: EVAP: readiness, Mode 06 3A/3C, Mode 0A permanent codes
steps.why: Only useful after an overnight cold soak with fuel below 85 %; do not clear anything.
steps.preconditions: Overnight cold soak, fuel below 85 % (was 88.6 %, note 7ada5cfedef3).

steps.title: Discovery sweep with identity re-read, then name and accept responders
steps.why: Do: sweep CAN-C with no cable, then name and accept responders. Call: POST /api/live/discover {bus: can_c, vin} (the sweep re-reads each responder's identity set F190 F187 F188 F189 F18C F191 F192 F194 F195, read-only); then, no car needed, GET /api/live/responders?vin=... (MCP name_responders) and POST /api/live/responders/accept {vin, address, module} (MCP accept_responder). Known conflict to settle: addresses.json already holds DTCM at target 1A, ESM at 1F and DASM at 2A from discovery on 2026-10-24/25; that disagrees with the DTCM 18DA29F1 note and puts DASM on the same byte as ABS (2A). The identity re-read must settle each one. Call accept_responder only for a responder whose identity matched a MES log line (the proposal names the log file and line); ambiguous or no match means no accept, and write down why. Done: DTCM, ESM, DASM, AFLS, PAM and HALF are each either 'confirmed (owner)' or have a stated reason they are not. Owner decides: every accept, after reading the proposal reason and log lines; a warning that the same target byte is already confirmed for another module must be read before going on.
steps.preconditions: Ignition on, engine off, plain adapter on CAN-C with no cable (declare cable none), MES closed, battery maintainer or healthy battery, doors closed so modules do not sleep mid-sweep. After the cold RFHUB read.

steps.title: Mode 06 read with layout check; shudder counters A1-A5
steps.why: Do: one unfiltered Mode 06 read that proves the 9-byte layout and also gives the misfire counters. Call: GET /live/obd/mode06 (MCP read_mode06) with no mids argument, so the supported bitmaps (06 00, 06 20, ...) are read; if A1-A5 are not in that result, repeat with mids=A1,A2,A3,A4,A5 (this one has no bitmap to check against). The response carries layout_check {ok, anomalies, saved_to}; the raw reply and verdict go to C:\ProgramData\cuore\mode06_layout_check\<timestamp>.json. Done: layout_check.ok is true with no anomalies, the saved file lists the records (keep it), and A1-A5 are recorded. If ok is false, read the anomalies and alternative_layouts_tried in the saved file: a better-fitting alternative means the layout, not the car, is wrong; do not edit mode06.py from one guess. Scaling stays unknown for any UASID not in mode06._UASID_TABLE. The cold EVAP 3A/3C read is its own entry and is not repeated here. Owner decides: whether a failed layout check needs a second read before anyone touches the parser.
steps.preconditions: After a 40-60 km/h light-throttle drive, then parked at warm idle, handbrake on; CAN-C on the OBD port directly (no blue A5 or grey A6 cable); MES disconnected.

steps.title: Service-value discovery, read-only
steps.why: Find which DIDs hold the service values; record the candidates, change nothing.
steps.preconditions: MES closed; engine off or idling.

steps.title: G003A ground: voltage drop, then wiggle test
steps.why: Measure stud/terminal to battery negative running, then with rear heater and blower on; photos before cleaning, then after.
steps.preconditions: Engine running; take photos BEFORE cleaning.

steps.title: Battery: read the label; in MES only read PROXI byte 63
steps.why: Record H7/H8, Ah and CCA from the label; no registration write.
steps.preconditions: Battery label visible; MES in read-only mode.

steps.title: Decode confirm, engine off: MES first (tags 1-2), then CUORE
steps.why: Do: record the same two static conditions in MES, then in CUORE, then compare 195B, 1925, 1926, 1009, 1959 and the throttle channels. MES and CUORE never share the adapter. MES: connect to the ECM (Magneti Marelli IAW 10JA), Graph tab, add Engine speed; Boost pressure; Desired boost pressure; Boost pressure signal; Throttle position (Track 1); Throttle position (Track 2); Throttle angle; Throttle position; Atmospheric pressure; Vehicle speed; Battery voltage; Fuel level; Engine oil temperature; Engine temperature; Air temperature (Boost/Manifold). CSV Start; ignition on, engine off, pedal up, press tag key 1, hold 20 s; pedal fully down and held, press tag key 2, hold 20 s; CSV Stop, note the saved file name, disconnect MES completely. CUORE: POST /live/session/start with channels engine_rpm, ecm_1000, ecm_1925, ecm_1926, ecm_195b, ecm_1959, ecm_195a, ecm_1956, barometric_pressure, ecm_1009, runtime_since_start, egr_temperature, throttle_position, vehicle_speed, ecm_1002, ecm_1955, fuel_level, ecm_1001, engine_oil_temp, ecm_1302; POST /live/record/start; same conditions in the same order, POST /live/record/tag 1 (pedal up) then 2 (pedal down), or the Live page tag buttons; POST /live/record/stop; POST /live/session/stop. Analyse: MCP decode_confirm_run(vin, mes_log_path, cuore_recording_path) in the default static mode, read GET /live/decode-confirm/runs?run_id=<id> (verdict, conditions compared, transform, reason per channel). MES CSV tag format is unverified: after this first tagged MES recording, open the CSV and confirm the TAG cell starts with the digit. A MES text log (FESLog_*.txt) has no tags and every channel would be no_data. The tags 3-4 half is the engine-running entry; this one is split from the design doc's single run so the engine state changes once. Done: a verdict per channel; confirmed needs agreement in at least 2 conditions with data, throttle candidates need tags 1 and 2 in both files, ecm_1009 and egr_temperature have no MES counterpart and stay no_data, a value identical in all conditions is ambiguous. Owner decides: each decode_confirm_accept(vin, run_id, channel) (a candidate pairing also needs confirm_pairing=true); results go to C:\ProgramData\cuore\did_overrides.json.
steps.preconditions: Engine warm, battery maintainer on, ignition on with engine off, pedal released at the start. Discovery entry finished (CUORE off the adapter) before MES connects.
steps.source: docs/design/DECODE_CONFIRM_SESSION.md; CUORE note ce54db3f26e5 and the 2026-10-26 cross-check findings

steps.title: CAN-C module code round: IPC, TCM, and ESM/DTCM if accepted
steps.why: Do: read codes and snapshots from IPC and TCM, and from ESM and DTCM only if the discovery entry accepted them. Call: GET /api/live/round?bus=can_c&vin=ZASFAKPN5J7B88115 (default modules IPC, TCM, ESM, DTCM; add modules=IPC,TCM to restrict). Per module it reads 19 02, then 19 04 and 19 06 for each code with a fault bit set, and stores every result as an observation. Done: IPC (0x60) and TCM (0x18) show read: true with a codes list; ESM and DTCM show read: true only if accepted, otherwise skipped with 'no confirmed address' (expected, not a failure); snapshots_raw counts 19 04 replies CUORE can only show as raw bytes; candidate_fields is empty for IPC and TCM (no scaffold). Owner decides: whether to run the c_first coverage baseline first (later passes are judged against it), and whether ESM and DTCM are included (only after their accept).
steps.preconditions: Ignition on, engine off, plain adapter on CAN-C (HS/MS on HS), cable declared none, MES closed or disconnected, CUORE recording and session from the decode entry stopped.

steps.title: Decode confirm, engine running: MES first (tags 3-4), then CUORE
steps.why: Do: the engine-running half of the decode confirm, same channels, same calls and same file handling as the engine-off decode entry. MES: Graph tab with the same 15 channels, CSV Start; engine idling warm, press tag key 3, hold 30 s; optional steady 2000 rpm, press tag key 4, hold 20 s; CSV Stop, note the file name, disconnect MES completely. Check the TAG cell of this CSV starts with the digit (format unverified until the first tagged recording is opened). CUORE: POST /live/session/start (same channel list), POST /live/record/start, tag 3 at warm idle and 4 at 2000 rpm with POST /live/record/tag or the Live page buttons, POST /live/record/stop, POST /live/session/stop. Analyse with decode_confirm_run on the new pair of files. Done: a verdict per channel from tags 3 and 4; a channel with no data in the second condition stays unconfirmed. Owner decides: whether to hold 2000 rpm (tag 4 is optional); each decode_confirm_accept (candidate pairings need confirm_pairing=true).
steps.preconditions: Engine running and warm, battery maintainer on, MES and CUORE never on the adapter together.

steps.title: CAN captures A, B and C with live rpm and speed
steps.why: Validates the opendbc signal decodings against this car.
steps.preconditions: Live rpm and speed visible while capturing.

steps.title: Grey cable: ABS code round (CAN-CH)
steps.why: Do: read ABS codes and snapshots on CAN-CH. WARNING pin 13: the vLinker FS can put 18 V on OBD pin 13, which is CAN-CH(-) on this car. Never issue a FEPS or programming-voltage command during this round. Steps: finish or skip c_first; continuity-check the grey A6 cable first (no short between pins 1 and 9); fit it and declare grey_a6. Call: GET /api/live/round?bus=can_ch&modules=ABS&vin=ZASFAKPN5J7B88115&confirm=true (confirm=true is required on CAN-CH; the response repeats the warning under warnings). Done: ABS (18DA2AF1) shows read: true; candidate_fields lists the seven unbound snapshot names; snapshots_raw above 0 is normal (ABS DID lengths are unknown). Then remove the cable and declare none. Owner decides: go or no-go on the continuity check, passing confirm=true, and when to skip c_first.
steps.preconditions: Ignition on; the design doc names no engine state for this round, so keep it as in the CAN-C round (engine off). MES closed. Cable swap checklist is the 'ch' pass in the coverage page.

steps.title: ABS snapshot binding: match MES numbers to CUORE raw values
steps.why: Do: name the ABS snapshot DIDs from numbers MES prints. In MES: Alfa Romeo Stelvio 2.0 Turbo 16V MultiAir > Continental ABS MK C1 > Read error codes (per-code environmental data: operating time, startups, brake switches, battery V, speed, hydraulic and pedal pressure); disconnect MES. Reference: FESLog_2609042001 (C104B-92: 12.1 V, 11.1 bar, 3.6 bar; U1700-87: 10.6 V, 2.6 bar, 0.0 bar). In CUORE open the same code: GET /api/live/module/ABS/dtc/<code>?vin=ZASFAKPN5J7B88115&confirm=true, read proposals and unresolved_did, match raw values to the MES numbers. Bind: POST /api/live/snapshot-bind {vin, module: ABS, did: <hex>, field_name: 'Battery voltage', length: <n>, unit: 'V', div: 10} (length and div only if known). Binding a DID with length lets the walk continue to the next DID; repeat. Done: no unresolved_did remains, or each remaining one has a stated reason; bindings are in C:\ProgramData\cuore\snapshot_bindings.json and show as 'bound (owner)'. Owner decides: each bind, only for numbers that match; length and div are not guessed.
steps.preconditions: abs-round done with the grey cable still fitted (whether MES needs it for ABS is not stated in the design doc; keep it fitted until the MES screen is read). MES and CUORE never on the adapter together.
